title: Add config diff schema + static validation rules for Optimize quality gates
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Internal: Optimize now uses a versioned ConfigDiff v1 payload and will reject unsupported/unsafe diffs before triggering eval-harness.
description: Context: Optimize recommendations (batching/caching/quantization profile changes) need to be gated by evals before they can be applied to production traffic. We’ve seen a few near-miss cases where an optimization proposal was syntactically valid but semantically unsafe (e.g., quant profile incompatible with model family + GPU SKU, or caching knobs that violate runtime invariants). This PR introduces a typed, versioned config-diff schema plus static validation and explicit rejection reasons so we can fail fast before spending GPU cycles running evals and before changes reach rollout controller. What’s in this PR: (1) ConfigDiff v1 schema: Adds a versioned diff payload used across Optimize -> eval-harness trigger -> audit log. We represent diffs as an explicit list of operations rather than "free-form JSON patches" to keep validation predictable and to make audit trails readable. The v1 payload is stable and backward-compatible within v1. (2) Static validation rules: Adds a server-side validator for config diffs that runs before eval execution. Validation covers syntax (required fields, enum validity), bounds/ranges, and cross-field constraints (e.g., batching policy constraints vs streaming mode, kv-cache constraints vs context window, quant profile constraints vs model family + runtime backend). (3) Rejection reason codes: Standardizes error codes returned to Optimize/Console so UI can display actionable failure reasons and link to docs/runbooks. These reason codes are also emitted to audit logs (without leaking customer prompt content). (4) Test coverage + fixtures: Unit tests for parsing/validation, plus golden fixtures for common diffs and expected failure modes. Schema overview (high level): - diff_version: "v1" - scope: route_id / model_id / deployment_tier (hosted|dedicated) - ops: list of typed operations (BatchingPolicyOp, KvCacheOp, QuantProfileOp) - baseline_ref: optional reference to baseline config id (required for certain change types; validated) Example (illustrative): {"diff_version":"v1","scope":{"route_id":"rt_8n3..."},"ops":[{"type":"BATCHING_POLICY","max_batch_tokens":8192,"max_wait_ms":8},{"type":"KV_CACHE","prefix_cache_enabled":true,"max_prefix_cache_entries":2000}],"reason":"optimize_recommendation","proposed_by":"optimize"} Validation rules (selected): - Common: reject unknown diff_version; require non-empty ops; enforce max ops count (currently 10) to keep reviews/audits readable. - BatchingPolicyOp: validate max_wait_ms within [0,50]; max_batch_tokens within per-model bounds; disallow max_wait_ms > 0 when route has "strict_latency" policy (pulled from route policy snapshot). - KvCacheOp: disallow enabling prefix cache if runtime backend does not support it for the route’s model family; enforce max_prefix_cache_entries <= 5000; if prefix_cache_enabled=false then max_prefix_cache_entries must be unset. - QuantProfileOp: require baseline_ref; validate profile exists; validate compatibility against (model_family, gpu_sku, backend) matrix; disallow switching to any profile marked "experimental" unless route gating policy allows it (flag + tier check). - Cross-op: reject diffs that modify both kv-cache and quant profile in the same diff for MVP (forces separate gate runs to simplify attribution); reject conflicting ops (multiple ops of same type). Rejection reasons (returned as code + short message): - INVALID_SCHEMA: missing/invalid fields, unknown op type, invalid enums. - UNSUPPORTED_CHANGE_TYPE: op type not allowed under current rollout (feature-flagged). - OUT_OF_RANGE: numeric bounds violated. - INCOMPATIBLE_WITH_RUNTIME: known incompatibility with backend/model/gpu. - UNSAFE_COMBINATION: cross-op conflict or forbidden combination. - BASELINE_REQUIRED: missing baseline_ref for ops that require it. - POLICY_VIOLATION: route/tier policy disallows this change (e.g., experimental quant). Integration notes: - Optimize service should call validateConfigDiffV1(diff, routePolicySnapshot) before triggering eval-harness (ENG-3922). - The validator returns a normalized diff (e.g., defaulted fields removed, canonical ordering of ops) to improve caching and audit diffs. - Console API will display error codes as-is; copy improvements are tracked separately. Backward-compat: This is a breaking change for internal callers that were sending untyped "config_patch" blobs to the Optimize service. We keep a temporary compatibility shim behind OPTIMIZE_ACCEPT_LEGACY_PATCH until 2026-02-01 (default off in prod; on in staging for migration). Testing: - Added unit tests for all op types + cross-op constraints. - Added property-ish fuzz tests for numeric bounds and unknown fields to ensure we don’t accept surprising payloads. - Updated existing Optimize recommendation tests to emit ConfigDiff v1 fixtures. Rollout plan: Merge behind feature flag OPTIMIZE_CONFIG_DIFF_V1_VALIDATE (enabled in staging by default; prod enablement will be paired with the eval-harness trigger PR rollout). Follow-ups: - Wire validator errors to audit log events (ENG-3927). - Consider allowing multi-op diffs after we have better attribution in gate artifacts. - Add a small docs page for reason codes and remediation suggestions (tracked in docs PR).

conversation: Noah Patel (review): Can we make the quant compatibility failure explicit vs bundling under INCOMPATIBLE_WITH_RUNTIME? We’ll want to distinguish "profile doesn’t exist" vs "exists but incompatible" for triage.
Benji Okafor (author): Good call. Split into QUANT_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND and QUANT_PROFILE_INCOMPATIBLE, both still map to a user-friendly message in Console. Updated validator + tests.
Olivia Grant (review): For eval-harness, we need normalized diffs to be stable across retries. Do we guarantee op ordering and omission of defaults?
Benji Okafor (author): Yes. Validator returns normalized payload: ops sorted by type, unset fields stripped, and defaults not serialized. Added a test that ensures stable JSON stringify across runs.
Jordan Lee (review): Policy snapshot usage looks fine, but ensure we don’t accidentally fetch live policy during validation (must be the same snapshot used for gate run).
Benji Okafor (author): Updated route handlers to pass the snapshot object explicitly; removed fallback to policy store. Added an assertion + logs when snapshot missing.
Michael Nguyen (review): Please include rejection code in structured logs and include diff hash (not full payload) for audit privacy.
Benji Okafor (author): Added diff_hash (sha256 of normalized diff) + rejection_code in logs. Payload only logged in debug mode in staging.
Noah Patel (approval): Approved after rejection code split + added invariant tests.
Olivia Grant (approval): Approved; normalization guarantee unblocks eval-harness contract work.
